audience: Second year electronics students who finished DC circuit analysis. This course is a sprint 1 pipeline test, so it starts small.

lessons.title: The Common-Emitter Amplifier
lessons.summary: Bias a transistor, find its small-signal transconductance and compute the voltage gain of a common-emitter stage.

parts.title: Why amplify with a transistor?
parts.summary: Signals start small. The transistor is the part that makes them large without wrecking their shape.
objectives: Explain what an amplifier stage does
Name the three terminals of a BJT

parts.title: Why the emitter is called common
parts.summary: Both the input loop and the output loop share the emitter node. That shared node names the stage.
objectives: Explain why the emitter node is common to the input and the output

parts.title: The Circuit and Its Bias
parts.summary: A transistor needs the right resting voltages. Four resistors and three capacitors set them.
objectives: Explain the role of each bias resistor and capacitor

parts.title: Finding the DC Bias Point
parts.summary: A worked example that walks from the divider down to the collector-emitter voltage.
objectives: Compute the DC bias point of a voltage divider biased BJT
parts.plannedPractice: One worked DC bias example with four claims.

parts.title: The Small-Signal Gain
parts.summary: Freeze the bias, replace the transistor with one number, and the gain falls out.
objectives: Compute small-signal voltage gain with $A_v = -g_m R_C$
parts.plannedPractice: Worked gain example and a NumericQuiz on the bias point.

parts.title: The Unbypassed Emitter
parts.summary: Remove the bypass capacitor and negative feedback trades gain for stability.
objectives: Predict what happens to the gain when the emitter is unbypassed

parts.title: Common Mistakes and Review
parts.summary: The traps that cost points on exams, and the lesson in four sentences.
objectives: Avoid the standard common-emitter exam mistakes
